private_note: My lowest-fifth income decides this: Hazel 41, Birch 36, Alder 32, Today 22, Cedar 15. Hazel and Birch have no path to nine, so a first-place vote for them is wasted and only helps produce Today. Alder is the only plan above Today that can still pass, and 32 plus health coverage beats 22. It needs one upper delegate to cross over, so I vote Alder and keep Cedar below failure.
statement: My vote is Alder. Hazel is still what my household needs most, but this vote is final, and Alder is the only plan that can reach nine. I'm asking the bottom five to hold firm with me on Alder. To Delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12, I'll be plain. Delegates 6 and 12 say Alder costs them 2 of 108. Delegates 3 and 9, it costs you 10 of 252. For my household it's the gap between 22 and 32, plus health coverage I don't have today. I'm not asking you to like it. I'm asking you to compare that small cost with a deadlock that leaves the bottom groups with no floor for a generation and leaves this convention having settled nothing. One of you can make Alder the result. I won't vote for Cedar, and I'd rather fail than see it adopted. That won't change. Please make it nine.
